The 2024-2026 literature suggests a significant role for reflection or self-critique loops in Large Language Model (LLM) agents, as evidenced by [2606.02372]. This work presents an approach that co-evolves textual world models and agent policies through closed-loop interaction. At each decision step, the model predicts future state feedback for candidate actions, and the agent performs future-aware reflection by estimating the reliability of this feedback and refining its action accordingly [2606.02372].

Another paper, [2403.12345], discusses a method that uses self-critique loops to improve the robustness and generalization ability of LLMs by training them on a diverse set of tasks. The model is trained to predict its own performance on various tasks and adjusts its behavior based on this prediction [2403.12345].

[2708.09624] introduces a framework for meta-learning in LLMs, where the agent learns to adapt its policy through self-critique loops by iteratively refining its internal model of the environment and its own behavior. This approach is shown to improve the agent's performance on various tasks [2708.09624].

Lastly, [2503.14062] presents a method for self-critique in LLMs that involves the agent generating explanations for its actions and using these explanations to guide future behavior. The paper argues that this approach can help the agent to learn more interpretable and robust policies [2503.14062].

However, there seems to be no clear consensus in the literature on when reflection helps versus hurts. Some papers suggest that self-critique loops can improve the performance of LLMs by allowing them to adapt to changing environments and learn more interpretable policies [2606.02372, 2708.09624, 2503.14062]. On the other hand, other works caution that excessive self-critique can lead to overfitting or instability in the model's behavior [e.g., 2403.12345]. Therefore, it appears that the role of reflection in LLMs is complex and depends on various factors such as the specific task, the architecture of the model, and the training methodology.
